source.title: Mitigating Position-Shift Failures in Text-Based Modular Arithmetic via Position Curriculum and Template Diversity

page_placements.theme: Held-out accuracy does not guarantee broader extrapolation

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses grokking as context but explicitly focuses on format robustness rather than delayed generalization. It neither tests nor relies on the delayed-grokking claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports modular-addition accuracy and format-robustness results, but does not report training accuracy or whether test accuracy rises long after overfitting. Its results therefore do not test any listed version. Rows below record its reported evaluation outcomes on the related algorithmic task; cited grokking results are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains character-level Transformers on text-rendered modular addition (p=97, 50% disjoint-pair split, 5000 AdamW steps, wd 0.01) and reports only final accuracies under position and template shift. It reports no training-accuracy curve, no train/test gap over time, no delay, no dataset-size sweep, no mechanistic analysis and no optimizer/numerical control. The authors state their focus is 'not the timing of delayed generalization per se'. Figure 2 shows training curves, but the text describes only robustness versus in-distribution success, not delayed generalization. No listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that high disjoint-pair accuracy can coexist with catastrophic position and template brittleness. They find that position curriculum, template diversity and consistency training substantially improve robustness. They frame this as explicit invariance training, complementary to and not accelerating classic grokking.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains character-level Transformers for robustness to position and template variation using curriculum, template mixtures, anchors, and multi-variant consistency loss; it does not reproduce the original delayed-generalization method.
record.method_sensitivity: Robustness depends on the training intervention: position-only steering improves Eval-B and Eval-C0, while adding template diversity improves Eval-C0 further. Positions 0 and 8, outside the curriculum range, remain much weaker for the position-steered models. The ALiBi-style positional-bias ablation performs poorly in this setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Baseline reaches 96.8% disjoint-pair accuracy but 14.9% under position shift and 1.2% on OOD templates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In text-rendered modular addition, strong held-out-pair generalization can coexist with severe brittleness to expression position and template format.

fits_no_version.finding: Position curriculum plus multi-variant consistency, and adding template diversity and anchors, raises position-shift and template-OOD accuracy within the trained position range.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit invariance training improves format robustness in algorithmic text tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing learned absolute positional embeddings with an ALiBi-style bias drops Eval-A to 21.4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned absolute positional embeddings aid character-level parsing in this setup.

record.problems: The task is narrow: single-step modular addition and a limited set of position ranges and template families. The study explicitly does not analyze delayed generalization timing. Reported results are means and standard deviations over three seeds; Eval-A uses n=400, Eval-C0/C1 use n=200, and each Eval-B position uses n=100.

untested.parts: No training accuracy, no timing of test-accuracy rise relative to training saturation, no training-set-size variation.
Only algorithmic data; no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
No weight-decay sweep, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No identification or comparison of learned algorithms across runs.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification is confirmed. Figure 2 training curves exist but are not quantified or discussed in terms of delayed generalization, so nothing in them can be extracted for V1. With 50% training data and only 5000 steps, no grokking delay is claimed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training accuracy, overfitting, a delayed test-accuracy rise, or how delay changes with training-set size.
No mechanistic circuit analysis or continuous progress measures.
Uses text-rendered modular addition only; does not test non-algorithmic data or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Does not test an efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction and Section 2 discuss grokking and describe invariance training as complementary to it.

tranche.reason: The study measures position and template robustness, without establishing delayed generalization or testing another listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The test_reason overstates the absence of dynamics: Section 5.2 and Figure 2 describe training curves. Nevertheless, the text does not establish a generalization delay relative to training-accuracy saturation.
